discovery: Squeezed states of light and their use to beat the quantum shot-noise limit in interferometric measurement
motivation: In 1981 Caves showed that the quantum noise of an interferometer comes from vacuum fluctuations entering its dark port, and that injecting squeezed vacuum could push sensitivity below the shot-noise limit that was then thought to be fundamental. Kimble's group produced strongly squeezed light from optical parametric oscillators and made quantum-noise-reduced measurements possible in practice. Schnabel turned squeezing into a robust, high-level technology: squeezing at audio-band frequencies, a squeezed-light source that has run continuously at GEO600 since 2010, and a world-record 15 dB of squeezing. Squeezed light is now used in every observing run of LIGO, Virgo and GEO600. It enlarges the observable volume of the universe and has let us reduce quantum noise in the motion of kilogram-scale mirrors. This line of work, from theory through laboratory to observatory, is one of the clearest cases of quantum mechanics being used to extend what can be measured.
